title: The Harms of Class Imbalance Corrections for Machine Learning Based Prediction Models: A Simulation Study
study_context: Monte Carlo simulations of prediction models and a MIMIC-III case study.
population_or_data: Monte Carlo simulations of prediction models and a MIMIC-III case study.
main_findings: In the examined machine-learning prediction settings, class imbalance corrections often overestimated risk; uncorrected models had similar or better calibration, and recalibration did not invariably remove the problem.
limitations: Selected-page review only: PDF p.1, Abstract. Text extracted and page visually checked on 2026-10-07.
Published article; PMC open-access copy, CC BY-NC-ND 4.0.
Transfer to cardiac WSI MIL requires qualification.
does_not_establish: Abstract review does not establish per-algorithm effect sizes, universal harm, applicability to neural WSI, or miscalibration of the SMC models.
relevance_to_project: Class correction should be evaluated rather than assumed beneficial, including its effect on calibration.
